doc_format: GENUINE OLD-STYLE EDGAR SGML TEXT -- verified concretely by reading the FY1995 10-K line by line. Structure: the entire filing (10-K body + all exhibits) is ONE flat .txt submission, internally delimited by <TYPE>/<SEQUENCE>/<DESCRIPTION> tags (<TYPE>10-K ... <TYPE>EX-10.1 ... <TYPE>EX-13 ... <TYPE>EX-21). Financial tables use literal SGML markup <TABLE><CAPTION><S><C>...<C> where <S> marks the stub/label column and each <C> marks one numeric column -- NOT HTML, no real table cells. Column alignment is achieved purely by whitespace padding (monospace-assumed rendering); numbers are right-aligned, $ signs appear only on the first/last row of a column block, negative numbers are parenthesized e.g. (39,141), blank cells (not '0', not 'N/A') represent nil/not- applicable. Horizontal rules under subtotals/above totals are literal ASCII dash and equals-sign lines (e.g. '- --------' -- note the leading space, an EDGAR SGML escaping quirk for lines starting with a dash). Page breaks are literal <PAGE> tags, a holdover from when 10-Ks were physically paginated documents. A parser for this era needs fixed-width/whitespace-column extraction (or naive regex on the <S>/<C> markers), NOT an HTML/DOM parser.
